clue.text: Nuts for a bird

definitions.meaning: nuts in the slang sense of crazy or mad
the European bird famous for laying eggs in other birds' nests

explanation.surface: Someone names a nut that is somehow fit to feed a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: slang for mad, and the name of a well-known migratory bird with a two-note call.

clue.text: Reject fish, laughing quietly

parts.note: to chuck something is to throw it out or reject it
the ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone throws back a fish they caught and has a quiet laugh about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a low, suppressed laugh is exactly this kind of quiet mirth.

clue.text: How anti-pollution campaigners aim to make big profit?

definitions.text: How anti-pollution campaigners aim to make big profit?

parts.words: How anti-pollution campaigners aim to make big profit?
parts.note: the phrase meaning to make a large profit also literally describes tidying away pollution, which is what such campaigners aim to do

explanation.surface: A question about green campaigners secretly chasing a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase is idiom for making a killing financially, and literally for removing dirt and waste.

clue.text: Kind of therapy almost everyone needed after hostile take-over

indicators.note: after places the word for a hostile take-over before the shortened word for everyone

parts.note: an occupation is a military seizure of territory, a hostile take-over

indicators.note: almost means the word for everyone loses its final letter

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: After a company is seized in a hostile bid, nearly every employee needs therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hostile take-over' suggests business, but it is the military seizure of a country. 'almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupational therapy is a recognised kind of rehabilitative treatment helping people manage daily tasks.

clue.text: Certainly not enjoying a night out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the words beside it are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone is definitely not having fun on their evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks part of 'a night out', but it is the anagram signal for A NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing something is the opposite of liking it, so you are certainly not enjoying it.

clue.text: Look left and see transport terminal

parts.note: an air is a look or manner, as in an air of confidence
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A traveller is told to look left and they will see the terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes are a form of transport and this is where their journeys start and end.

clue.text: Woman featured in Cheshire newspaper

indicators.note: featured in says the name is contained within the run of the following words

explanation.surface: A woman appears in a local paper in the county of Cheshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is an English county in the north-west. The name sits across the join of CheshIRE NEwspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Supposed visitor should be given a hearing

indicators.note: being given a hearing means the word is spoken and the answer sounds like it

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A guest is supposed to be listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to have supposed something is to have conjectured it without proof.

clue.text: Allotment scheme

definitions.meaning: a small piece of land allotted for growing vegetables

explanation.surface: An allotment scheme, as a council might run.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a small patch of ground for gardening, and a secret plan or conspiracy.

clue.text: Fellow discovered form of nuclear energy

indicators.note: a form of something reshapes it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the standard symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A man discovers a new type of nuclear power.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's given name, so it can stand for a fellow.

clue.text: Foreign cheeses said to give you mild wind

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken, and the answer sounds like them

parts.note: bries are soft French cheeses

explanation.surface: Eating imported cheese gives someone gentle flatulence.
explanation.definitionFit: A light gentle wind outdoors is a synonym; the surface plays on wind in the stomach.

clue.text: Ill-fated soldiers ordered to carry equipment after daybreak

indicators.note: after places the soldiers' unit after the word for daybreak

parts.note: first light is daybreak

indicators.note: to carry means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to order
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Doomed troops are ordered to carry their kit at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Light Brigade made the disastrous Charge of 1854 in the Crimean War, hence 'ill-fated'.
explanation.definitionFit: The British cavalry unit famously destroyed in a doomed charge, so soldiers with an unhappy fate.

clue.text: Be determined to reject all time-servers?

definitions.text: Be determined to reject all time-servers?

parts.words: Be determined to reject all time-servers?
parts.note: time-servers is read as people serving time in jail; refusing to capture such people is the literal reading of an idiom for being ruthless

explanation.surface: A boss resolves to get rid of all the people just clocking time.
explanation.walkthrough: A time-server usually means someone lazily waiting out their job; here it is a convict serving time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting ruthlessly and with total determination, literally sparing no captives.

clue.text: Do away with military report

definitions.meaning: to kill or get rid of
an official report sent from the front

explanation.surface: Someone wants to scrap a report from the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to kill someone off, and an official message sent from a battlefield.

clue.text: Journalist of the Year, perhaps, was a heavy drinker

parts.note: an award of the year marks the best one, the top
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: An award-winning journalist turns out to have been a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: To tope is an old word for drinking alcohol to excess.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to drink alcohol habitually and to excess, so its past tense is a heavy boozer's habit.

clue.text: Appearing on high structure topless servant makes quite a display

indicators.note: in a down clue appearing on means the servant stands above, before, the next piece

parts.note: a page is a young servant

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the structure is removed

parts.note: a gantry is a high frame bearing signals or a crane

explanation.surface: A half-naked servant appearing on a high structure makes quite a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' looks like it describes the servant, but it removes the G of GANTRY, leaving ANTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate ceremonial show and splendour is a grand spectacle, a lavish display.

clue.text: Father, say, is engaged in risky activity?

indicators.note: engaged in means placed inside another word

parts.note: a bet is a gamble, a risky activity
EG, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A dad, for instance, takes up a dangerous pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a noun but is the verb, to sire a child.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to father and to sire mean the same: to produce offspring.

clue.text: Be upset to finish school

definitions.meaning: to be overcome with emotion, to lose composure
British schools are said to do this when term ends for the holidays

explanation.surface: A pupil is upset at the end of school.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a school is said to break up at the end of term.
explanation.definitionFit: Two idioms: to go to pieces emotionally, and for a school to close at the end of term.

clue.text: Ill-starred merchants

indicators.note: ill means badly formed, so the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: Merchants doomed to misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-starred' reads as one word meaning unlucky; split it and 'Ill' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: people who buy and sell goods are dealers.

clue.text: Old composer going round ten universities

indicators.note: going round means the pieces surround the next one

parts.note: Frank Bridge was an English composer, teacher of Britten
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: An elderly composer tours ten universities.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the joint name for Oxford and Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend of two names standing for England's two oldest universities together.

clue.text: Wretched soldier picked up old gold coin

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means the word is lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
a noble was an old English gold coin

explanation.surface: A miserable soldier picks up an antique gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and dishonourable, so contemptible or wretched.

clue.text: It's the end for this sort of clue!

definitions.text: It's the end for this sort of clue!

parts.words: It's the end for this sort of clue!
parts.note: the clue ends with a punctuation symbol, and that symbol always ends exclamatory sentences

explanation.surface: A remark that this is the last of such clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol placed at the close of an exclamatory sentence, as in the clue itself.

clue.text: Hot food one leaves to cool

indicators.note: leaves means the letter goes out of the word

parts.note: chilli is a hot, spicy dish or pepper
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Hot food that one leaves out to cool down.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the last I from CHILLI gives the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to make something cold, as in refrigerating it.

clue.text: Generous daughter supporting family

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means the daughter sits below the family word

parts.note: kin are family

explanation.surface: A generous daughter helps to support her family.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: giving and considerate toward others.

clue.text: Stabbed gruesome fiend with tip of dirk

indicators.note: the tip of the dagger is its point, its last letter
gruesome signals the letters of fiend are mangled

explanation.surface: A gruesome fiend stabs someone with the point of a dagger.
explanation.walkthrough: A dirk is a Scottish dagger; its tip is its end letter K.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: wounded with a blade.

clue.text: Talk to new teacher, at first

indicators.note: at first places the teacher before the other pieces

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

explanation.surface: Someone is told to talk to a new teacher first.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang for chattering on at length, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom meaning to chatter at length, from rhyming slang, so a synonym of talk.

clue.text: Foreign language buff

definitions.meaning: to buff is to rub something until it shines

explanation.surface: A foreign-language enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the tongue spoken in Warsaw, and to rub a surface to a shine.

clue.text: Source of sherry endlessly offered to my lad

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the town is dropped

parts.note: Jerez in Andalusia is the Spanish town that gives sherry its name

explanation.surface: Sherry from its home town is offered without end to my boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's given name, so an example of a lad.
